title: All shop supplies, including a hand-typed amount, go to the Labor row
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have two active staff members at the test location with their "Sales Representative" switch on: sales rep A and sales rep B.
  • Use a customer with no Sales Representative assigned.
  • Make sure the test location's Shop Supplies Charge is 10% of labor and nothing else is invoiced at the test location today.
  • Have a work order for that customer with one labor line of 2.00 hours at $100.00 an hour and one part sold at $50.00, Labor set to sales rep A and Parts set to sales rep B.
  • On the work order's Finance tab, type the shop supplies by hand as $15.00 in place of the calculated $20.00, then invoice the work order today.
  • Open Reports > Sales By Representative in a desktop browser at least 1024 pixels wide, with the date range set to today and the Sales Type column turned on.
custom_steps:
1. Expand sales rep A.
  2. Expand sales rep B.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The work order's invoice has a "Labor" row under sales rep A that shows Shop Supplies $15.00, the amount typed by hand.

Step 2:

  • Its "Parts" row under sales rep B shows a dash under Shop Supplies.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R4: “A Labor row is credited with Labor Invoiced, Labor Margin, labor-line fees and discounts, Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Labor Delta and all of the invoice's Shop Supplies, including an amount typed by hand.”
  • S5-R15: “On a Labor row the parts columns show a dash, and on a Parts row the labor, hours and Shop Supplies columns show a dash, not $0.00. $0.00 is shown only for a real zero. A row that holds both sides, one person on both, keeps the report's rule that an invoice with no labor shows Labor Delta 0.0.”
  • Key Decisions, shop supplies: “Shop supplies go to the Labor side. ShopView calculates shop supplies from the labor total, so the whole charge, including an amount typed by hand, is credited to Labor. Whole-invoice fees and discounts are shared by the size of each side. Fees and discounts on a part line or a labor line already belong to that side.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Claude design canvas "Splitting Sales Representatives" (https://claude.ai/artifact/8MHqwyffAYtqZ6EccS5RUm), page 4 (cited by the story), export read 19 Oct 2026, used for on-screen labels; the look itself is checked in the "Design — how it looks" cases.
